pages.title: Readwise Help
pages.description: Help center for Readwise and Reader, covering setup, highlight import, Daily Review, Reader content import, reading customization, annotations, FAQs, feature guides, and tools.
pages.summary: Help center for Readwise and Reader, covering setup, highlight import, Daily Review, Reader content import, reading customization, annotations, FAQs, feature guides, and tools.

content.text: Readwise focuses on organizing, managing, exporting, resurfacing, and retaining highlights.
Reader is the all-in-one reading application that integrates with Readwise.
The recommended starting workflow is to import highlights, configure Daily Review, add content to Reader, customize the reading experience, and begin highlighting and taking notes.

pages.page_title: How are Readwise and Reader related?
pages.title: How are Readwise and Reader related?
pages.description: Explains the product split and shared account/database relationship between Readwise and Reader.
pages.summary: Explains the product split and shared account/database relationship between Readwise and Reader.

content.text: Readwise and Reader are separate applications.
Readwise manages and resurfaces highlights; Reader manages and reads articles, books, and other documents.
The same account works in both apps.
Reader highlights and notes sync to Readwise automatically.
Externally purchased books cannot generally be imported into Reader unless a DRM-free EPUB is available, and importing an EPUB does not retain highlights made on the original platform.

pages.title: Web Apps
pages.description: Documents the Readwise and Reader web applications and shared authentication behavior.
pages.summary: Documents the Readwise and Reader web applications and shared authentication behavior.

content.text: Readwise web app is available from readwise.io/dashboard.
Reader web app is available from read.readwise.io.
Reader and Readwise use the same account and authentication.

pages.title: Mobile Apps
pages.description: Documents Readwise and Reader mobile availability on iOS and Android.
pages.summary: Documents Readwise and Reader mobile availability on iOS and Android.

content.text: Readwise has iOS and Android apps.
Reader has iOS and Android apps.
Reader on Android can run on Android-based e-ink devices such as Onyx BOOX.
Reader iOS documentation states support for devices running iOS 13.0 or later.

pages.title: Desktop Apps
pages.description: Documents native Reader desktop applications.
pages.summary: Documents native Reader desktop applications.

content.text: Reader provides native macOS and Windows applications in addition to its web app.

pages.title: Account FAQs
pages.description: Account-wide documentation covering access, subscription and billing, taxes and invoices, and privacy/security.
pages.summary: Account-wide documentation covering access, subscription and billing, taxes and invoices, and privacy/security.

content.text: Readwise and Reader share a single account, subscription, and data system.

pages.title: Account Access
pages.description: Covers shared authentication, Apple ID login, password changes, and account access behavior.
pages.summary: Covers shared authentication, Apple ID login, password changes, and account access behavior.

content.text: Readwise and Reader share the same account and authentication system.
Logging into one app also authenticates access to the other.

pages.title: Subscription & Billing
pages.description: Covers the paid subscription model, discounts, referrals, receipts, and billing.
pages.summary: Covers the paid subscription model, discounts, referrals, receipts, and billing.

content.text: Readwise does not offer a permanent free plan after the free trial.
Subscriptions can be billed monthly or annually.

Discounts may be available for students, teachers, non-profits, military, first responders, and users in developing countries or depressed-currency regions when purchased through the Readwise website.
Receipts are available from readwise.io/receipts.

pages.title: Taxes & Invoices
pages.description: Explains sales tax, VAT, GST, invoice tax handling, business exemptions, billing information, and tax refunds.
pages.summary: Explains sales tax, VAT, GST, invoice tax handling, business exemptions, billing information, and tax refunds.

content.text: Applicable taxes depend on jurisdiction, address, and business status.
Business users in some jurisdictions may qualify for tax exemption by providing a valid tax identifier.
Billing information can be updated through the subscription management flow.

pages.title: Privacy & Security
pages.description: Documents AI-data handling and the absence of end-to-end encryption.
pages.summary: Documents AI-data handling and the absence of end-to-end encryption.

content.text: Readwise states that data sent through its OpenAI API usage is opted out of training.
Readwise and Reader do not support end-to-end encryption.
The documentation positions the products as consumer software optimized for user experience rather than enterprise-compliance or national-security use cases.

pages.title: What is Readwise Reader?
pages.description: Reader is an all-in-one reading application for articles, newsletters, EPUBs, PDFs, videos, tweets, podcasts, and other content, with annotations synced to Readwise.
pages.summary: Reader is an all-in-one reading application for articles, newsletters, EPUBs, PDFs, videos, tweets, podcasts, and other content, with annotations synced to Readwise.

content.text: Reader unifies multiple digital content formats in one reading environment.
Highlights and notes created in Reader sync automatically to Readwise.
Recommended starting actions include importing content, using the browser extension or share sheet, subscribing to RSS, customizing appearance, and annotating while reading.

pages.title: Saving Content to Reader
pages.description: Guide to saving content through the browser extension and mobile share sheet.
pages.summary: Guide to saving content through the browser extension and mobile share sheet.

content.text: The browser extension can save articles and optionally highlight the open web.
The extension is considered the most robust web-save method because it can access rendered page content rather than only the URL.
On mobile, the share sheet can save content and expose actions such as Read Now, delete, tags, document note, and moving to Later or Shortlist.

pages.title: Migrate Existing Content to Reader
pages.description: Official migration guide for moving content from other read-it-later and feed services into Reader.
pages.summary: Official migration guide for moving content from other read-it-later and feed services into Reader.

content.text: Reader provides migration paths for existing libraries from supported services.
Instapaper can be connected from Reader integrations and its content mapped into Reader locations.
Pocket direct migration is no longer available after Pocket shutdown, but previously exported Pocket ZIP files can still be uploaded.

pages.title: Organizing Content
pages.description: Guide to organizing Reader content using locations, tags, filtered views, and related tools.
pages.summary: Guide to organizing Reader content using locations, tags, filtered views, and related tools.

content.text: Reader is organized around a flat document database plus query-driven views.
Tags and filtered views can be used together to build dynamic organizational systems.

pages.title: Basics
pages.description: Reader basics: platforms, login, offline use, command palette, keyboard shortcuts, progress indicators, undo, deletion, and restore.
pages.summary: Reader basics: platforms, login, offline use, command palette, keyboard shortcuts, progress indicators, undo, deletion, and restore.

content.text: Reader is available on web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and major browsers through extensions.
Reader supports offline use on web if opened before going offline and through native desktop/mobile apps with cached documents.
Selective offline caching is configurable by section; Feed is not cached by default.
The web app has a Command Palette at Cmd/Ctrl+K and extensive keyboard shortcuts.
Deleted documents go to Trash and can be restored; Trash behavior is device-specific according to the documentation.

pages.title: Adding Content to Reader
pages.description: Ways to save content: browser extension, mobile share sheet, upload, URL-save format, podcasts, Twitter, and RSS-related flows.
pages.summary: Ways to save content: browser extension, mobile share sheet, upload, URL-save format, podcasts, Twitter, and RSS-related flows.

content.text: Library holds manually curated documents; Feed holds automatically pushed content such as RSS/newsletters.
Browser extension default save shortcut is Alt+R.
Reader supports file uploads including PDF, EPUB, Markdown, and OPML; web upload uses drag-and-drop or the U shortcut.
Most uploaded files are limited to 500 MB, while Markdown files are limited to 10 MB.
A URL can be saved using the wise.readwise.io/save?url= format.
Podcast links can be saved to obtain transcripts; Reader is intentionally a podcast companion rather than a full podcast player.

pages.title: Appearance
pages.description: Reader appearance, typography, dark mode, side panels, pagination, long-form reading view, and two-column tablet reading.
pages.summary: Reader appearance, typography, dark mode, side panels, pagination, long-form reading view, and two-column tablet reading.

content.text: Appearance controls include typeface, font size, line spacing, and web-only line width.
Font size is documented as adjustable from 14px to 80px, defaulting to 20px.
Reader supports light, dark, and automatic theme modes.
Reader supports per-document right-to-left text direction.
Reader uses vertical paged scrolling, with optional horizontal/two-column pagination on supported tablet layouts.
Long-form reading view is enabled for EPUBs by default.

pages.title: Feed (RSS, Newsletters, Twitter Digests)
pages.description: RSS/feed subscription, OPML import, folders, seen state, incomplete feed content, feed views, and refresh behavior.
pages.summary: RSS/feed subscription, OPML import, folders, seen state, incomplete feed content, feed views, and refresh behavior.

content.text: Reader Feed is used for automatically delivered content such as RSS feeds and newsletters.
OPML can be uploaded to migrate RSS subscriptions.
Feed content can be marked seen and organized into feed folders.
Manual refresh is available on web via browser refresh and on mobile via pull-to-refresh.

pages.title: Filtered Views
pages.description: Reader's core query-based organizational system.
pages.summary: Reader's core query-based organizational system.

content.text: Reader describes the account as one flat database of documents with Filtered Views used to query subsets.
Clicking authors, tags, or RSS sources creates filtered views on those attributes.
Filtered Views can be saved, pinned, assigned emoji icons, and optionally display count badges.
Mobile can create query-based filtered views from Search using the plus button.

pages.title: Highlights, Tags, and Notes
pages.description: Keyboard annotations, auto-highlighting, image highlights, open-web highlighting, document notes, tags, stylus use, copy/edit, and bulk actions.
pages.summary: Keyboard annotations, auto-highlighting, image highlights, open-web highlighting, document notes, tags, stylus use, copy/edit, and bulk actions.

content.text: On web, paragraph focus is moved with arrow keys; H highlights, T tags, and N adds a note.
Auto-highlighting immediately converts selected text into a highlight and can be toggled.
Reader supports image highlighting.
Document tags and highlight tags are separate and do not inherit from one another.
Bulk Actions apply actions to all documents in a filtered/list view; Reader does not currently provide arbitrary multi-select for documents.
Reader currently supports a single highlight color; tags are suggested when users need a workflow classification system.

pages.title: Text-to-Speech (TTS)
pages.description: TTS playback, controls, languages, AirPods/headphone gestures, web support, and offline limitations.
pages.summary: TTS playback, controls, languages, AirPods/headphone gestures, web support, and offline limitations.

content.text: TTS can read most Reader documents; PDFs require text view for playback.
TTS can start from the current reading position.
TTS supports multiple languages.
TTS requires an internet connection and cannot currently be used offline.
Web shortcuts include P for play/pause, Shift+P for stop, arrow keys for skipping, and comma/period for playback speed.

pages.title: Searching
pages.description: Full-text library search, offline fallback, in-document search, and current search limitations.
pages.summary: Full-text library search, offline fallback, in-document search, and current search limitations.

content.text: Reader search covers full text plus titles and authors for Library documents.
Server-based Better Search searches the entire Library and falls back to on-device search while offline.
Feed documents are not currently indexed for full-text search.
In-document search uses Cmd/Ctrl+F on web/desktop and Find in document on mobile.
Filtered views and full-text search are currently separate features.

pages.title: Sharing
pages.description: Public annotated links, bundles, highlight sharing, printing, and annotated PDF download.
pages.summary: Public annotated links, bundles, highlight sharing, printing, and annotated PDF download.

content.text: Reader can create public links for annotated documents, but certain uploaded documents such as EPUBs and PDFs cannot be publicly shared for privacy/copyright reasons.
Public links can be disabled.
Bundles are shareable collections based on filtered views and require manual refresh to publish newly added documents.
Highlights can be shared as images.
Annotated documents can be printed; annotated PDFs can be downloaded with annotations.

pages.title: YouTube Videos
pages.description: YouTube playback with synchronized transcripts, shortcuts, transcript enhancement, captions, and channel subscriptions.
pages.summary: YouTube playback with synchronized transcripts, shortcuts, transcript enhancement, captions, and channel subscriptions.

content.text: Saved YouTube videos can be watched alongside time-synchronized transcripts.
Space plays/pauses, comma and period change speed, and arrow keys skip 15 seconds.
Enhanced transcripts can improve auto-generated YouTube caption quality.
Changing transcript language can create a separate Reader document.
YouTube channel URLs can be added as feeds.

pages.title: PDFs
pages.description: PDF metadata, zoom, highlights, annotations, export, text mode, dark mode, and limitations.
pages.summary: PDF metadata, zoom, highlights, annotations, export, text mode, dark mode, and limitations.

content.text: Reader supports original PDF view and enhanced/text view.
PDF text view enables standard Reader appearance customization and auto-highlighting.
PDF text extraction can contain line-break artifacts.
Reader can download highlighted PDFs with annotations.
Some PDF/stylus capabilities differ between original view and text view.

pages.title: Parsing
pages.description: Troubleshooting incomplete article parsing and recommended save methods.
pages.summary: Troubleshooting incomplete article parsing and recommended save methods.

content.text: Reader does not claim perfect parsing of the open web.
Browser-extension saves and iOS Safari share-sheet saves generally yield the highest-quality parsing because they can provide full rendered content.
Parsing problems can be reported from Reader while the affected document is open.

pages.title: Exporting
pages.description: Reader highlight export, tagged highlight export, CSV/OPML/full-content export, and sending documents to Kindle.
pages.summary: Reader highlight export, tagged highlight export, CSV/OPML/full-content export, and sending documents to Kindle.

content.text: Reader highlights sync to Readwise and then can be exported to supported note-taking integrations.
Per-document annotations can be copied to clipboard or downloaded as Markdown.
Markdown export templates are customizable with Jinja2-style variables.
Tagged highlight collections can be exported from their tag view.

pages.title: Ghostreader FAQ
pages.description: Ghostreader automation, auto-summarization, auto-tagging, model/API-key behavior, and prompt customization.
pages.summary: Ghostreader automation, auto-summarization, auto-tagging, model/API-key behavior, and prompt customization.

content.text: Auto-summarization and auto-tagging are configured from Ghostreader preferences.
Documents manually saved to the Library can be automatically summarized by default; Feed auto-summarization requires a user-provided OpenAI API key.
Custom prompts are edited on web and can be used on mobile.

pages.title: Miscellaneous
pages.description: Feedback, API discovery, extension roles, deletion behavior, roadmap/known-issue guidance, and tagged-highlight location.
pages.summary: Feedback, API discovery, extension roles, deletion behavior, roadmap/known-issue guidance, and tagged-highlight location.

content.text: Reader feedback can be submitted from the Command Palette or mobile Support and feedback action.
Reader exposes a public API at readwise.io/reader_api.
Deleting a Reader article can remove associated Reader highlights from the shared Readwise/Reader database; archiving annotated documents is recommended for preservation.
Different Readwise browser extensions serve different purposes, including Kindle sync, export authentication, and Reader saving/highlighting.

pages.title: Importing Content to Reader
pages.description: FAQ covering migration/import from read-it-later and feed services.
pages.summary: FAQ covering migration/import from read-it-later and feed services.

content.text: Reader supports importing content from multiple existing reading services and file-based exports.
Import behavior varies by source and may map source folders/statuses into Reader locations.

pages.title: Reader Feature Guides
pages.description: Index for filtering, Ghostreader, and workflow guides.
pages.summary: Index for filtering, Ghostreader, and workflow guides.

pages.title: Filtering
pages.description: Index for query syntax, query examples, and default filtered views.
pages.summary: Index for query syntax, query examples, and default filtered views.

pages.title: Filtering Syntax Guide
pages.description: Detailed query language for Reader Filtered Views.
pages.summary: Detailed query language for Reader Filtered Views.

content.text: Queries support AND, OR, and parenthetical nesting.
Date parameters include saved, last_opened, published, and last_status with before/after operators.
Text parameters include tag, domain, url, category/type, location/in, title, and saved_using.
Document categories include article, epub, email, pdf, tweet, rss, video, and podcast.
Boolean parameters include feed, seen, and shared.
Numeric parameters include words, progress, highlights, minutes, and saved_count.
The has parameter can test for highlights, tags, and notes.

pages.title: Filtered View Examples
pages.description: Ready-to-use Reader query examples.
pages.summary: Ready-to-use Reader query examples.

content.text: Examples include short reads, currently reading, untagged documents, email subscriptions, old Feed cleanup, YouTube Shorts filtering, and unfinished long reads.
Example short-reads query: minutes__lt:10 AND in:later.
Example untagged query: has__not:tags.
Example video-length query: category:video AND minutes__gt:2.

pages.title: Default Filtered Views
pages.description: Default category and utility views with their backing queries.
pages.summary: Default category and utility views with their backing queries.

content.text: Default Library category queries include category:article, category:epub, category:email, category:pdf, category:tweet, category:video, and category:podcast.
Deleted default category views can be recreated using their exact default query.

pages.title: Learn about Ghostreader
pages.description: Index for Ghostreader overview, chat, prompts, prompt library, reference, and tips.
pages.summary: Index for Ghostreader overview, chat, prompts, prompt library, reference, and tips.

pages.title: What is Ghostreader?
pages.description: Overview of Reader's AI-powered reading assistant.
pages.summary: Overview of Reader's AI-powered reading assistant.

content.text: Ghostreader can summarize documents, define or look up terms, translate passages, explain concepts, and run custom prompts.
On web/desktop Ghostreader prompt responses are integrated into the Chat interface.
Shift+G invokes document-level prompts; G operates on selected text.
On mobile, short selections can open Quick Lookup.

pages.title: Chat with your documents
pages.description: Reader document chat with source-aware context and follow-up questions.
pages.summary: Reader document chat with source-aware context and follow-up questions.

content.text: Document Chat uses the document, metadata, reading position, and conversation history as context.
Useful chat responses can be saved to the document note field or copied.
The documented default chat model is GPT-5.1 with low thinking, with a more thoughtful option available.

pages.title: Quick Lookup
pages.description: Mobile-only inline define, lookup, and translate panel.
pages.summary: Mobile-only inline define, lookup, and translate panel.

content.text: Quick Lookup is available in the Reader mobile app and triggers on selections of one to three words.
It offers Define, Lookup, and Translate tabs.
Quick Lookup requires Ghostreader to be enabled and requires an internet connection.

pages.title: Default Ghostreader Prompts
pages.description: Explains the built-in Ghostreader prompt set.
pages.summary: Explains the built-in Ghostreader prompt set.

content.text: Built-in prompts cover definitions, translation, simplification, summarization, and other reading-assistance tasks.
Default prompt settings, including model selection, are configurable in Ghostreader preferences.
The documented default model for preset prompts is GPT-5 Mini.

pages.title: Ghostreader Prompt Customization
pages.description: Guide to building custom Ghostreader prompts and understanding scopes.
pages.summary: Guide to building custom Ghostreader prompts and understanding scopes.

content.text: Custom Ghostreader prompts can operate at different scopes such as full document or selected text.
Prompt customization is based on templates and document/selection variables.

pages.title: Ghostreader Prompt Library
pages.description: Curated examples of custom prompts for use and experimentation.
pages.summary: Curated examples of custom prompts for use and experimentation.

content.text: The library provides copyable prompt examples for tasks such as flashcards, vocabulary, etymology, translation, summaries, and transformations.

pages.title: Ghostreader References
pages.description: Reference for Ghostreader variables, subroutines, and utilities.
pages.summary: Reference for Ghostreader variables, subroutines, and utilities.

content.text: Variables include document author, category, content, domain, length, title, source, summary, tags, note, language, progress, highlights, HTML, key sentences, and selection context.
Subroutines include central_sentences, central_paragraphs, classify, document_range, lexical_search, most_similar, num_tokens, and truncate.
Utilities include set, length, join, input, and response.

pages.title: Ghostreader Tips & Tricks
pages.description: Advanced techniques for prompt behavior and auto-tagging.
pages.summary: Advanced techniques for prompt behavior and auto-tagging.

content.text: The {# noghost #} flag can prevent Ghostreader from running when document rules do not match.
The flag applies to the entire prompt and should not be mixed with prompt branches that require LLM execution.

pages.description: Workflow guide index for favorites, library configuration, long-form reading, and AI recommendations.
pages.summary: Workflow guide index for favorites, library configuration, long-form reading, and AI recommendations.

content.text: Reader workflow documentation demonstrates how configuration, tags, filters, and AI tools can be combined for custom reading systems.

pages.title: Favorites Workflow
pages.description: Use tags and dynamic queries to create a collection of high-signal documents.
pages.summary: Use tags and dynamic queries to create a collection of high-signal documents.

content.text: A favorites system can use a manual favorite tag, dynamic highlight-count queries, or both.
Queries can account for document length/type when defining what counts as high-signal.

pages.page_title: How to choose a Library configuration
pages.title: How to choose a Library configuration
pages.description: Explains Reader Library configurations and how they change triage locations.
pages.summary: Explains Reader Library configurations and how they change triage locations.

content.text: Reader offers multiple Library configurations to match different reading workflows.
Queries and location values should match the active Library configuration, such as Inbox/Later/Archive versus Later/Shortlist/Archive.

pages.title: Long-form Reading Workflow
pages.description: Workflow for treating books and long-form documents as first-class reading material.
pages.summary: Workflow for treating books and long-form documents as first-class reading material.

content.text: Long-form reading workflows can combine EPUB/PDF organization, paged scrolling, long-form reading view, progress tracking, TTS, and annotation.

pages.title: Reading Recommendations with Readwise MCP
pages.description: Use Reader/Readwise data plus an AI client to recommend what to read next.
pages.summary: Use Reader/Readwise data plus an AI client to recommend what to read next.

content.text: MCP-based prompts can recommend unread, older, unfinished, time-bounded, topic-specific, or type-specific documents from a user's Reader library.

pages.title: What is Readwise?
pages.description: Readwise helps retain and organize reading insights through resurfacing, spaced repetition, active recall, Daily Review, exports, and search.
pages.summary: Readwise helps retain and organize reading insights through resurfacing, spaced repetition, active recall, Daily Review, exports, and search.

content.text: Readwise uses Daily Reviews to resurface highlights.
The product uses spaced repetition and active recall concepts.
Readwise can import highlights from many sources and export to note-taking systems.

pages.title: Readwise General FAQs
pages.description: General Readwise questions including supplemental highlights, ordering, email import authorization, and API discovery.
pages.summary: General Readwise questions including supplemental highlights, ordering, email import authorization, and API discovery.

content.text: Supplemental Highlights can seed Daily Review for users with few personal highlights.
Highlight order may depend on source metadata; sources without a location identifier may be ordered by highlight creation time.
Readwise exposes a public API.

pages.title: Reviewing Your Highlights
pages.description: Daily Review configuration, frequency tuning, audio review, related highlights, review modes, keyboard shortcuts, soft discard, Mastery algorithm, and Themed Reviews.
pages.summary: Daily Review configuration, frequency tuning, audio review, related highlights, review modes, keyboard shortcuts, soft discard, Mastery algorithm, and Themed Reviews.

content.text: Frequency Tuning can adjust how often source types and individual documents appear in Daily Review.
Daily Review supports audio playback.
Review Mode shows highlights one at a time; Scroll Mode displays a collection on one page.
Readwise uses soft Discard to avoid re-importing highlights from connected sources.
Mastery uses a recall-probability half-life model; documented initial half-lives are 7 days for Soon, 14 days for Later, and 28 days for Someday.
A Mastery item becomes a resurfacing candidate when estimated recall probability decays to 50% or lower.

pages.title: Finding Your Highlights
pages.description: Browse, keyword search, URL-based search, and AI chat for locating prior highlights.
pages.summary: Browse, keyword search, URL-based search, and AI chat for locating prior highlights.

content.text: Readwise supports browsing highlights by source/category.
Keyword search uses highlight text and document metadata.
The search page accepts a q URL parameter.
Chat With Highlights can surface semantically relevant highlights when exact wording is unknown.

pages.title: Readwise Discord Bot
pages.description: Discord bot commands for saved links, server feed aggregation, and RSS.
pages.summary: Discord bot commands for saved links, server feed aggregation, and RSS.

content.text: The Discord bot can expose a server-specific feed aggregator URL and RSS feed URL via slash commands.
Reader users can subscribe to the generated RSS feed.

pages.summary: Index for Themed Reviews, Action Tags, Mastery, and Chat With Highlights.

pages.title: How to Create a Themed Review
pages.description: Create reusable, scheduled/custom review sets of selected highlights.
pages.summary: Create reusable, scheduled/custom review sets of selected highlights.

content.text: Themed Reviews can be based on topics, documents, tags, or other source selections.
Themed Reviews can be edited or deleted.
They can be used for topical study, skill building, problem solving, writing, or other custom review workflows.

pages.title: How to Use Action Tags
pages.description: Special highlight-note syntax for concatenation, inline tagging, headings, and other actions.
pages.summary: Special highlight-note syntax for concatenation, inline tagging, headings, and other actions.

content.text: Action tags begin with a period.
Concatenation uses .c1, .c2, and subsequent numbered tags to combine non-adjacent highlights.
Inline tags convert dot-prefixed notes into Readwise highlight tags.
Heading tags use .h1, .h2, .h3 hierarchy.

pages.title: How to Increase Retention with Mastery
pages.description: Readwise active-recall/spaced-repetition study feature with Q&A and cloze cards.
pages.summary: Readwise active-recall/spaced-repetition study feature with Q&A and cloze cards.

content.text: Mastery supports Q&A cards.
Mastery supports cloze-deletion cards.
The .qa Action Tag can be combined with a Ghostreader prompt in Reader to create Q&A cards while reading.

pages.title: Chat With Your Readwise Highlights
pages.description: AI chat across a user's Readwise highlight corpus.
pages.summary: AI chat across a user's Readwise highlight corpus.

content.text: Chat With Highlights provides semantic search and question answering across the highlight library.
Chats can be renamed and deleted.
External AI clients can access highlights via the Readwise MCP.

pages.description: Overview of automatic and manual highlight import methods.
pages.summary: Overview of automatic and manual highlight import methods.

content.text: Supported import approaches include platform integrations, CSV upload, freeform input, email, and OCR scanning.

pages.summary: Kindle sync via Readwise browser extension and manual handling for personal documents.

content.text: Purchased/borrowed Kindle highlights can sync through the Readwise extension.

workflows.workflow_name: Save web article with Reader extension

steps.action: Install the official Reader browser extension.
Open the desired article.
Activate the extension or press Alt+R.
Optionally add notes/tags or highlight on the open web.

Choose filter criteria.
Compose a query using documented parameters/operators.

workflows.purpose: Ask questions or run AI prompts while reading.

steps.action: Open the Chat panel or use Shift+G for document-level prompts.
Choose a preset prompt or ask a custom question.
Review the AI response.
Ask follow-up questions if useful.
Save a valuable response to the document note or copy it.
Open Ghostreader preferences on web.
Choose an existing prompt to edit or create a new prompt.
Select the prompt scope.
Use document/selection variables and optional subroutines/utilities.
Choose the model where supported.
Save and test the prompt.
Open Readwise Import and choose Kindle.
Install/authorize the Readwise Kindle browser extension.
Sign in to Amazon when prompted.
Allow the extension to visit the Kindle notebook and sync highlights.
Keep the extension installed for background/ongoing sync if desired.
Open Add Highlights in the Readwise mobile app.
Choose Add via photo.
Photograph or select an existing page image.
Adjust the selection and OCR text.
Add page number/notes and choose the book.
Save the highlight.
Open Configure Reviews / Frequency Tuning or access frequency controls from Library/Review.
Choose a source type or individual document.
Adjust frequency.
Observe resulting review mix and retune if needed.

workflows.purpose: Turn a highlight into active recall.

steps.action: Open the Mastery editor for a highlight.
Choose Q&A or Cloze Deletion.
Write the question/answer or select the cloze content.
Save the card.
Review it as the recall probability decays.
Open the Readwise Export page.
Choose Markdown.
Optionally enable custom formatting.
Edit Jinja2 templates for page title, metadata, highlights, and sync notifications.
Generate/download the export.

workflows.workflow_name: Connect an AI client with Readwise MCP
workflows.purpose: Give an AI app access to Readwise/Reader.

steps.action: Use the official MCP endpoint https://mcp2.readwise.io/mcp.
Add Readwise as a connector/plugin/MCP server in the chosen client.
Authorize access using the browser flow.
Use the exposed search/read/write tools from the AI client.
Run npm install -g @readwise/cli.
Run readwise login for browser OAuth, or login-with-token for headless usage.
Run readwise --help to inspect commands.
Use Reader/Readwise commands directly or through an AI coding agent.

limitations.details: Most uploaded files are limited to 500 MB; Markdown files are limited to 10 MB.

limitations.constraint: DRM-protected books cannot generally be imported
limitations.details: Books from ecosystems that do not provide a DRM-free EPUB cannot be imported into Reader as full books.
Text-to-speech requires network access because speech is generated on request.
Quick Lookup is available in the Reader mobile app; web/desktop uses Chat or Ghostreader prompts.

limitations.constraint: Feed is not indexed for Reader full-text search
limitations.details: Feed documents become searchable after moving them to Library.

limitations.constraint: Full-text search and Filtered Views are separate
limitations.details: The documentation describes merging them as a roadmap item rather than current behavior.

limitations.constraint: Multiple Reader highlight colors are not supported
limitations.details: Reader recommends tags for workflow classification instead.
Finer-grained keyboard highlighting is documented as a future roadmap item.

limitations.constraint: Some uploaded document types cannot be publicly shared
limitations.details: Certain user-uploaded documents such as EPUBs and PDFs do not support public annotated links.

limitations.constraint: Web parsing is not guaranteed perfect
limitations.details: Reader explicitly states that the open web cannot be parsed 100% correctly 100% of the time.

limitations.constraint: Public API docs use access-token authentication
limitations.details: Public API documentation uses Authorization: Token <access_token>; a complete third-party OAuth contract is not documented on the public API reference.
The official privacy documentation states that Readwise and Reader do not support end-to-end encryption.
Pocket shut down July 8, 2025 and its API was later disabled; only previously exported data remains importable where documented.

contradictions.topic: Ghostreader model references differ by feature/page.

conflicting_sources.claim: Preset prompts documentation describes GPT-5 Mini as the default preset-prompt model.
Document Chat documentation describes GPT-5.1 with low thinking as its default chat model.

contradictions.resolution: These appear to describe different Ghostreader execution modes (preset prompts versus document Chat), so the knowledge base keeps them separate rather than treating them as a single global model setting.
